statement.text:
Let lFitX be the local Fitting class generated by a set of groups X and let Ψ(G)
be the smallest normal subgroup of a finite group G such that lFit(Ψ(G)∩M ) = lFitM
for every M ◁◁ G (K. Doerk, P. Hauck, Arch. Math., 35, no. 3 (1980), 218–227). We
say that a Fitting class F is saturated if Ψ(G) ∈ F implies that G ∈ F. Is it true that
every non-empty soluble saturated Fitting class is local?                N. T. Vorob’ëv
